title: Publish stable workspace APIs while preserving the completed pilot interfaces
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md, docs/DESIGN_RECONCILIATION.md and the referenced frozen docs/design sources. Rules Spec v1 is canonical: Repair/Sabotage each end at six, one direct player-card vote, private Route/Gate inputs and authoritative deterministic outcomes. The five-point/Witness/demo scripts and completed T01-T10 APIs are historical; preserve their existing tests/API compatibility without using them as new game rules. Edit only owned paths and use existing dependencies unless manifest ownership explicitly permits reviewed additions. Keep engine production pure and do not read credentials, provision services, deploy, publish PRs or start agents. Use original synthetic fixtures and verified assets only. Run scoped tests/lint/typecheck and npm run check; report outcomes and contract changes. Expose the implemented RNG, lobby, deck, legacy command/snapshot and theme/control modules through explicit package exports, preserving their names and declarations. Define a versioned module-subpath export convention so later owned modules can be imported across workspaces without direct relative source imports. Do not export symbols that do not exist yet. Verify emitted JavaScript and declaration compatibility, including the existing index/deck initialization relationship. This task coordinates baseline APIs; it does not implement new game behavior or silently convert the legacy transport schema into v1. Later producers may publish only their explicitly owned v1 symbols under the approved convention.
acceptance: Implemented package APIs can be consumed from the package root with correct declarations and no import-time side effects.
T01–T10 tests and API shapes remain valid; production v1 uses a distinct versioned path and schema.
Cross-package imports respect package exports and do not pull Firebase or browser code into the pure engine.
Consumer tests verify built JavaScript and emitted types, and the workspace lock graph remains valid.
